definition: A cancellation test is a neuropsychological assessment task that uses a target-cancellation measure as part of evaluating cognitive function. In this packet, it appears as the Multiple Feature Target Cancellation Test and is used particularly in the assessment of attention-related difficulties.

reasons: The packet only shows that the Multiple Feature Target Cancellation Test was one of several neuropsychological tests used in a post-COVID-19 study; it does not support the broader definitional claim that a cancellation test is generally a neuropsychological assessment task used to evaluate cognitive function.

The packet does not support the added characterization that the test is used particularly for attention-related difficulties; it only reports that some participants had persistent attention symptoms and that attention was among the domains of measurable change.
The definition goes beyond the packet by generalizing from one study to a generic test definition and by implying a specific clinical use that is not established here.

The packet only states that the “Multiple Feature Target Cancellation Test” was used as one of several neuropsychological tests in an outpatient assessment; it does not define what a “cancellation test” is, what “target-cancellation measure” means, or the general purpose of cancellation tests.

The definition claims it is used “particularly in the assessment of attention-related difficulties,” but the packet does not link the cancellation test specifically to attention assessment (it only reports that attention-related symptoms were commonly self-reported and that overall neurocognitive alterations were relevant to attention/working memory, without attributing this to the cancellation test itself).
The definition’s explanation of the sense/meaning of “cancellation test” is not directly supported by the packet’s text.
